gaps.where: Settings → Products → New product / pick an item → Save / Archive
gaps.gap: manage_product.prepare destructures `items` from product.list, which answers `{ products }`. So `items` is undefined, and `items.find(...)` throws a TypeError on every action (create, change, archive) before the card is drawn. The `.catch` only covers a rejected query, not a wrong shape. Nothing else can reach product.create, product.update or product.archive: none of them is in SCREEN_ACTIONS. So the Assistant cannot add, reprice or archive any item, and no test calls manage_product.
gaps.fix: In apps/worker/src/assistant/tools-settings-money.ts:343-346, use `const { products } = await query<{ products: Product[] }>(db, ctx, 'product.list', { includeArchived: true })` and then `products.find((p) => p.id === args['productId'])`. includeArchived matters because archive and change name items that may already be archived. Add apps/worker/test coverage that prepares and commits create, change and archive through manage_product.

gaps.where: Settings → Partners → a partner → Their link (Copy their link); phone: Share their link
gaps.gap: The screen and the phone both build the full link: the business's own domain when it is verified and its certificate is ready, otherwise the web app's address, plus linkPath. The Assistant's only source is read_partner_get, which hands over partner.get's bare `linkPath` (`/book/c/<calendarId>?ref=<code>`), while the tool's description (taken from the query's) calls it a 'link'. get_settings partners drops linkPath altogether. Nothing in prompt.ts or context.ts gives the business's public origin, and the prompt's own link example is https://handsfreeos.com/book/acme, so the model will guess the domain. runScreenRead never gets webUrl: createToolExecutor has it (tools-write.ts:861) but calls runScreenRead(db, tool, args, ctx) without it.
gaps.fix: Pass `webUrl` from createToolExecutor into runScreenRead (tools-write.ts:878). For partner.get, replace `partner.linkPath` with `partner.link = origin + linkPath` (null when linkPath is null). Work out the origin the way tools-forms.ts:380-388 does (branded_domain.get: verified and certificateReady gives https://<domain>, else webUrl), or reuse the worker's existing publicOrigin(tx, workspaceId, webUrl) in apps/worker/src/hosting/origin.ts:75 rather than writing a new helper. Make readArea take webUrl too, and add `link` to each partner in the partners `partnerList` shape (tools-settings.ts:174-195). Add a settings-map partners howTo: 'Copy a partner’s link: Settings → Partners → the partner → Their link → Copy their link'.

gaps.gap: GoHighLevel is the only source, and there is no sign-in: SIGN_IN_SOURCES is []. gaps.where: A partner's page (What they’ve earned, up to 200 lines; Their clients; Payouts last); an import's page (Rows that did not import, up to 100 with their data); a migration's page
gaps.gap: Real: runScreenRead slices any answer over 16,000 characters of JSON mid-string and tells the model to 'ask it for less (a smaller page, a narrower search)'. partner.get, import.get and migration.get take no limit or page, so it can't. partner.get returns up to 200 commissions (about 270 characters of JSON each) ahead of `payouts`. A partner with more than about 50 commissions loses their payout account ('Hasn’t set up payouts yet' / 'Their bank is in …') and their payout lines. import.get returns up to 100 failed rows, each with the whole raw CSV row, so a wide sheet shows only its first few failures, as a broken JSON fragment. The import's errorCount comes first and survives. Wrong: 'part of the clients list' is lost only when the clients list alone passes 16,000 characters, since `clients` comes before `commissions` in PartnerGetOutput. The migration page was not shown to overflow.
gaps.fix: In apps/worker/src/assistant/tools-screen-reads.ts:44-54, shorten long arrays before serialising rather than slicing text. Walk the result, cut each array to the first N items with a sibling `{ shown, total }`, and shrink N until JSON.stringify fits MOST. Then the model always gets valid JSON, and the later keys (`payouts`) survive. Alternatively, cap commissions for the Assistant (for example 30), and drop `raw` from import.get errors for the Assistant, keeping rowNumber and message.
